case_text:
Vignette:
A 35-year-old man is referred by his primary care physician for psychiatric evaluation after presenting with a 2-month history of persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities he previously enjoyed including playing guitar and socializing, insomnia with early morning awakening, decreased appetite with an unintentional 14-pound weight loss, difficulty concentrating at work, and pervasive feelings of worthlessness. He describes his mood as an overwhelming heaviness that does not lift. He has been increasingly isolating from friends and family. He denies suicidal ideation, hallucinations, or delusions. He has no prior psychiatric history. He went through a significant relationship breakup 3 months ago. Vital signs are normal. On mental status examination, he is casually dressed with poor grooming. Psychomotor retardation is present. Speech is soft and slow. Affect is flat. Thought process is linear but impoverished. PHQ-9 score is 22 indicating severe depression.
